title.fr: Fractures de l'extrémité distale du radius

classification.name: AO/OTA 2R3
classification.basis: PA and lateral radiographs centred on the wrist; CT for the articular pattern. A = extra-articular (A2 simple, qualified by dorsal or volar tilt; A3 wedge or multifragmentary metaphysis), B = partial articular (B1 radial styloid, B2 dorsal rim, B3 volar rim), C = complete articular (C1 simple articular and metaphyseal, C2 simple articular with multifragmentary metaphysis, C3 multifragmentary articular).

types.summary: Simple metaphyseal fracture with dorsal tilt and shortening; joint surface intact.
types.recommendation: Closed reduction and a moulded cast first: in DRAFFT2 K-wires did not improve 12-month PRWE over a cast, although 13% of the cast group needed fixation for loss of position. Under 65, fix if shortening >3 mm or dorsal tilt >10° persists; use K-wires when closed reduction holds, a volar locking plate when it does not (DRAFFT: equal 12-month function, plate gives faster early recovery). At 65 or older, a cast is first line.

types.summary: Extra-articular fracture with the distal fragment displaced and tilted volarly.
types.recommendation: Volar-displaced fractures are unstable in a cast; consider open reduction and a volar plate, which buttresses the fragment as well as fixing it.

title.ar: خارج المفصل، متعددة الشظايا في الكردوس

types.summary: Extra-articular fracture with a wedge or comminuted metaphysis, usually dorsal; prone to collapse after reduction.
types.recommendation: Comminution makes K-wires and casts lose length; if surgery is chosen, a volar locking plate is the usual fixed-angle option. Use bridging fixation when comminution runs into the shaft or bone is too poor to hold screws. At 65 or older, nonoperative treatment gives similar long-term results.

title.es: Articular parcial, estiloides radial (fractura del chófer)
title.ar: مفصلي جزئي، الناتئ الإبري الكعبري (كسر السائق)
title.fr: Articulaire partielle, styloïde radiale (fracture du chauffeur)
title.it: Articolare parziale, stiloide radiale (frattura dello chauffeur)

types.summary: Sagittal split through the scaphoid fossa detaching the radial styloid (radial column).
types.recommendation: Undisplaced: cast. Displaced: it is an articular fracture, so reduce to a step under 2 mm; K-wires or a cannulated screw through a small radial incision when closed reduction is achieved, a radial column or volar plate when it is not.

title.ar: مفصلي جزئي، قص الحافة الظهرية (كسر بارتون الظهري)
title.fr: Articulaire partielle, cisaillement marginal postérieur (Barton postérieur)
title.it: Articolare parziale, frattura marginale dorsale (Barton dorsale)

types.summary: Dorsal rim fragment sheared off with the carpus subluxing dorsally.
types.recommendation: Unstable fracture-subluxation: open reduction and dorsal buttress fixation (low-profile dorsal or fragment-specific plate) through the third–fourth compartment approach. Evidence is technique-level only.

title.ar: مفصلي جزئي، قص الحافة الراحية (كسر بارتون الراحي)
title.fr: Articulaire partielle, cisaillement marginal antérieur (Barton antérieur)
title.it: Articolare parziale, frattura marginale volare (Barton volare)

types.summary: Volar rim fragment, often including the volar lunate facet, sheared off with the carpus subluxing volarly.
types.recommendation: Unstable in a cast: volar buttress plate through the FCR approach. The plate must capture the volar lunate facet, or the fragment and carpus displace volarly (Harness); use a distal rim plate or supplementary wire or hook fixation for a small facet fragment.

title.en: Complete articular, simple articular and metaphyseal
title.de: Vollständig artikulär, einfach artikulär und metaphysär
title.es: Articular completa, articular y metafisaria simple
title.fr: Articulaire complète, articulaire et métaphysaire simple
title.it: Articolare completa, articolare e metafisaria semplice
title.nl: Volledig articulair, eenvoudig articulair en metafysair

types.summary: Simple articular split (often radial styloid plus lunate facet) with a simple metaphyseal fracture.
types.recommendation: Under 65, operate if the step is >2 mm or tilt or shortening exceed the thresholds. If closed manipulation reduces the joint, K-wires; if not, ORIF with a volar locking plate. At 65 or older, a cast is first line.

title.en: Complete articular, simple articular, metaphyseal multifragmentary
title.de: Vollständig artikulär, einfach artikulär, metaphysär mehrfragmentär
title.es: Articular completa, articular simple, metafisaria multifragmentaria
title.ar: مفصلي كامل، بسيط مفصلياً ومتعدد الشظايا كردوسياً
title.fr: Articulaire complète, articulaire simple, métaphysaire plurifragmentaire
title.it: Articolare completa, articolare semplice, metafisaria pluriframmentaria
title.nl: Volledig articulair, eenvoudig articulair, metafysair multifragmentair

types.summary: Simple articular split with metaphyseal comminution that removes the cortical buttress.
types.recommendation: If surgery is chosen, use a volar locking plate with subchondral distal screws to hold length over the comminuted metaphysis; K-wires alone tend to collapse. Fixation techniques give similar 12-month results; the plate gives earlier recovery.

types.summary: Comminuted joint surface (die-punch, central impaction, separate volar and dorsal lunate facets), with or without metaphyseal comminution.
types.recommendation: Get a CT. In active patients, the extended FCR approach with a volar locking plate reaches most fragments. Add dorsal or fragment-specific fixation only for a dorsal fragment that cannot be reduced or held from volar: in a 5-year RCT, combined plating had worse motion and PRWE and twice the hardware removal. Use a bridging plate or external fixator when the joint cannot be reconstructed. At 65 or older, the AAOS evidence against routine surgery still applies.

workup: PA and lateral radiographs centred on the wrist; document the mechanism, skin, circulation and median nerve sensation at presentation.

Measure on PA: radial inclination (normal about 22°), radial height (about 11 mm), ulnar variance (compare with a PA of the other wrist); on lateral: volar tilt (normal about 11°), and the teardrop angle (about 70°; a low angle means the volar lunate facet is displaced).
Post-reduction films decide management: re-measure shortening, dorsal tilt and articular step against the thresholds (>3 mm, >10°, >2 mm).
CT for intra-articular fractures before choosing an approach: die-punch or central impaction, size of the volar and dorsal lunate facet fragments, sigmoid notch, dorsal comminution.
Progressive or severe median nerve symptoms after reduction suggest acute carpal tunnel syndrome, which needs urgent decompression; don't confuse it with stable contusion paraesthesia.
Look for DRUJ instability, a displaced ulnar styloid base, carpal fractures and a widened scapholunate interval.
Judge functional demand rather than age alone. In a WRIST secondary analysis, activity level and comorbidities predicted who benefits from surgery better than chronological age did.
Assess falls risk and bone health and refer to fracture liaison.

decide.text: At 65 or older, surgery does not improve long-term patient-reported outcomes over nonoperative treatment (AAOS, strong). CROSSFIRE, Hassellund, VOLCON and WRIST all found no clinically important difference at 12–24 months. Plating gives faster early recovery and more patient-rated satisfaction. In DRIFT (2025), plating of fractures that would not reduce gave a 9.6-point PRWE benefit, below the 11-point MCID. Consider surgery for active, high-demand patients or severe deformity.

Under 65, operative treatment improves radiographic and patient-reported outcomes when post-reduction shortening is >3 mm, dorsal tilt >10° or intra-articular step >2 mm (AAOS, moderate). Weigh ulnar variance, step, tilt and the patient's needs.

Dorsally displaced fractures: manipulation and a moulded cast first. If fixation is needed, K-wires when the joint is intact or reducible closed; ORIF when it is not (NICE NG38). DRAFFT: K-wires and volar plate equal at 12 months and 5 years. DRAFFT2: K-wires no better than a cast after manipulation. Cochrane on pinning: low-certainty evidence.

Choice of fixation for unstable or complete articular fractures: no significant difference in 12-month radiographic or patient-reported outcomes between techniques; volar locking plates give better function at 3 months (AAOS, strong). In WRIST, external fixation and pinning had pin-site infection rates around 25%.
Volar-displaced fractures (Smith, volar Barton) are unstable and should be considered for open reduction and plate fixation.

Timing: within 72 hours of injury for intra-articular fractures and within 7 days for extra-articular ones; within 72 hours of the decision for re-displacement. Repeat radiographs at 1–2 weeks only where the fracture is unstable and re-displacement would lead to surgery.

Arthroscopic assistance does not change outcomes (AAOS, moderate). Combined volar and dorsal plating of type C fractures should be used sparingly: worse 5-year motion and PRWE, more hardware removal and later return to work than volar plating alone.

approaches.name: Volar FCR (modified Henry) approach, volar locking plate
approaches.when: A2-volar, B3 and most dorsally displaced A2, A3, C1 and C2 fractures that need open fixation.
approaches.position: Supine with a radiolucent hand table, arm abducted and supinated, upper-arm tourniquet. C-arm from the end of the table so that PA, true lateral, tilted lateral and skyline views can be taken without moving the limb.
approaches.incision: Longitudinal over the FCR tendon, from the distal wrist crease 6–8 cm proximally; angle radially across the crease if more distal exposure is needed.
approaches.interval: Open the FCR sheath and go through its floor with FCR retracted ulnarly (it shields the median nerve); the radial artery lies radial to the sheath. Sweep FPL ulnarly to expose pronator quadratus; release it in an L from its radial and distal borders, staying proximal to the watershed line and leaving the volar radiocarpal ligaments intact.

atRisk.why: Runs ulnar to FCR. Stay inside the FCR sheath and do not dissect on its ulnar side.

Lies ulnar and deep to FCR, under the FDS and FPL mass; injured by retractors or hooks levered on the ulnar side. Decompress the carpal tunnel separately if acute carpal tunnel symptoms were present before surgery.
Radial to the FCR sheath; incise the sheath floor, not its radial wall, and keep the artery with the radial flap.
Rubs on a plate left at or beyond the watershed line (Soong grade 1–2) and can rupture late. Place the plate proximal to the line and remove it if a prominent plate is symptomatic.
Releasing it from the radial border gives the exposure; repair over the plate is optional because evidence for benefit is weak.

The volar extrinsic radiocarpal ligaments arise distal to the watershed line. Do not release the volar capsule to see the joint, or the carpus can translate ulnarly; judge the joint on fluoroscopy instead.
Distal screws that pass the dorsal cortex near Lister's tubercle cause EPL attrition rupture. Measure, downsize by about 2 mm and check the skyline view.

steps: Clear the fracture and haematoma; restore length with traction and the volar cortex as the reduction key. An intrafocal K-wire levered through the fracture corrects dorsal tilt, and a radial styloid wire holds radial height and inclination.
Hold provisionally with K-wires; leave the volar cortex key-aligned so that the plate's anatomic contour brings back volar tilt.
Fix the plate to the shaft through the oblong hole and adjust its height on a true lateral: proximal to the watershed line, centred on the radial shaft.
Reduce the plate to the bone. For residual dorsal tilt, fix distally first parallel to the joint and then bring the plate down to the shaft.
Fill the distal row with subchondral locking screws or pegs: ulnar screws support the lunate facet, radial screws the styloid. Shorten them 2 mm from the dorsal cortex measurement.
Test DRUJ stability in pronation, neutral and supination after fixation.
implants: Anatomic volar locking plate (2.4 mm or 2.5 mm system, fixed or variable angle).
Smooth pegs or unicortical locking screws in the distal row where dorsal tines are at risk.
Distal rim or hook plate, or K-wire or tension-band supplementation, for a small volar lunate facet fragment.
checks: PA: radial inclination about 22°, radial height about 11 mm, ulnar variance restored to match the other side, articular step under 2 mm.

Tilted lateral (forearm raised about 20–25°, 23° in Soong's study): volar tilt toward the normal 11° and at least neutral, teardrop angle about 70°, distal ulnar-sided screws subchondral and out of the joint.
Tilted PA or oblique for the radial styloid screw, which the low-angle tilted laterals miss (Soong 2008); several oblique views are needed.
Dorsal tangential (skyline) view, wrist fully flexed with the beam along the forearm: no screw tip proud of the dorsal cortex, especially in the third and fourth compartments.
True lateral: plate edge proximal to the volar rim (watershed line), Soong grade 0.

approaches.name: Extended FCR approach (pronation of the proximal fragment)
approaches.when: C2 and C3 fractures and dorsal comminution needing intrafocal debridement, impacted central fragments, and fractures over 10–14 days old with early callus.
approaches.position: As for the FCR approach: supine, hand table, tourniquet, C-arm from the end.
approaches.incision: FCR incision, extended a little proximally.
approaches.interval: Go through the FCR floor as above, then release the radial septum and the brachioradialis insertion from the radial styloid in the floor of the first compartment. Pronate the proximal fragment out of the way (the 'book' opening) to see the fracture from inside: dorsal comminution, impacted articular fragments, dorsal callus.

atRisk.why: Emerges from under brachioradialis about 9 cm proximal to the styloid and runs radially over the first compartment. Stay deep on bone when releasing brachioradialis and retract with blunt instruments.
Mobilise it radially with its venae comitantes before the radial septum release; it is the structure most at risk when pronating the shaft.
APL and EPB in the first compartment lie directly over the brachioradialis insertion. Release subperiosteally beneath them without opening their sheath.
Its pull is the deforming force on the radial styloid; releasing it helps restore radial height. Do not cut far proximally, where the SBRN emerges.

steps: Release the radial septum and brachioradialis insertion; pronate the proximal radius to open the fracture.
Debride the fracture and lift impacted articular fragments against the scaphoid and lunate as a template, under fluoroscopy; graft or fill the metaphyseal defect if needed.
Supinate back, reduce the shaft to the distal block and hold with K-wires.

Apply the volar locking plate as in the FCR approach, with subchondral support for each column. Add a separate radial column or dorsal fragment-specific implant only if a fragment cannot be held from volar.
implants: Optional radial column plate, dorsal ulnar-corner pin plate, bone graft or substitute for the metaphyseal void.
checks: Same targets as the FCR approach.
Articular step and gap under 2 mm on PA and tilted lateral; CT or 3D fluoroscopy if unclear.
Skyline view for dorsal screw length.
DRUJ stability and sigmoid notch congruity.

approaches.name: Dorsal approach through the third–fourth compartment (fragment-specific or dorsal plate)
approaches.when: B2 dorsal Barton, dorsal die-punch or dorsal lunate facet fragments that cannot be reduced or held from volar, and the dorsal half of a combined approach for C3.
approaches.position: Supine, hand table, forearm pronated on the table, tourniquet; C-arm from the end.
approaches.incision: Longitudinal dorsal incision in line with Lister's tubercle and the third metacarpal, 6–8 cm, centred on the radiocarpal joint.
approaches.interval: Open the extensor retinaculum over the third compartment and transpose EPL radially. Elevate the fourth compartment subperiosteally ulnarly and the second compartment radially, without opening their sheaths. For articular viewing, use a ligament-sparing dorsal capsulotomy.

atRisk.why: Lies in the third compartment against Lister's tubercle. Free and transpose it out of the third compartment, and leave it outside the retinaculum at closure so it does not rub on the plate.
Terminal branch lies in the floor of the fourth compartment on the radial side. It is often divided (PIN neurectomy) during the approach; if it is preserved, protect it.
The fourth compartment tendons sit directly on a dorsal plate. Use low-profile plates, keep them under the retinaculum or periosteum, and expect tenosynovitis or rupture if implants are prominent.
Radial skin flap; avoid raising it with sharp dissection or traction near the radial styloid.
Divide it as little as possible during capsulotomy and repair it to avoid dorsal carpal instability.

steps: Expose the dorsal rim and Lister's tubercle; remove the tubercle flush if a plate needs to lie flat.
Reduce the dorsal rim or lunate facet fragment against the carpus under direct vision or through the capsulotomy.
Buttress with a low-profile dorsal plate (intermediate column) or fragment-specific plates (dorsal ulnar corner and radial column), following the column concept.
Close the retinaculum with EPL left outside it, subcutaneous.
implants: Fragment-specific implants: radial column plate, dorsal ulnar pin plate, wire forms.
Lag screws for a single dorsal rim fragment.
checks: Lateral: carpus reduced under the radius with no dorsal subluxation, dorsal rim congruent, volar tilt about 11°.
PA: radial inclination about 22°, radial height about 11 mm, articular step under 2 mm.
No screw entering the joint or the DRUJ.

approaches.name: Closed reduction and percutaneous K-wire fixation
approaches.when: A2-dorsal and C1 fractures that reduce closed but will not hold in a cast; displaced B1 radial styloid fractures.
approaches.position: Supine, hand table, finger-trap traction optional. Tourniquet is usually not needed. Mini or standard C-arm.
approaches.incision: Stab incisions with blunt spreading down to bone and a drill guide or soft-tissue sleeve. The radial styloid wire goes in through the snuffbox region between the first and second compartments; dorsal wires go in ulnar to Lister's tubercle between the fourth and fifth compartments.
approaches.interval: Percutaneous. Wires enter between the extensor compartments, not through them.

atRisk.why: Crosses the radial styloid area. Use a mini-open incision with spreading and a sleeve for styloid wires; transfixion causes painful neuroma.
Wires next to Lister's tubercle can tether or spear EPL. Keep dorsal wires ulnar to the tubercle and check thumb IP extension before you leave theatre.
First-compartment tendons. Enter dorsal to them or between the first and second compartments.

steps: Closed reduction: traction, then flexion and ulnar deviation over the distal fragment.
Intrafocal (Kapandji) wire into the dorsal fracture line, levered to restore volar tilt and then driven into the volar cortex.
Two radial styloid wires crossing the fracture into the far ulnar cortex of the shaft; a dorsal-ulnar wire for the lunate facet.
Bend and cut the wires outside the skin, or bury them; protect with a cast; remove at 4–6 weeks.
implants: Smooth K-wires (1.6–2.0 mm), two or three in total.
Cannulated screw as an alternative for an isolated styloid fragment.
checks: PA: radial inclination about 22°, radial height restored to within about 3 mm of the other side's ulnar variance, any step under 2 mm.
Lateral: dorsal tilt no more than 10°, ideally neutral to the normal volar tilt.
Wires bicortical but not long; no wire crossing the DRUJ.

approaches.name: Bridging external fixation or dorsal spanning (bridge) plate
approaches.when: Unreconstructable C3 or highly comminuted A3 fractures, osteoporotic bone that will not hold distal screws, severe soft-tissue injury or open fractures (staged), and polytrauma where the patient needs to bear weight through a crutch or frame (spanning plate).
approaches.position: Supine, hand table, tourniquet for the plate; C-arm from the end.
approaches.incision: External fixator: two short open incisions over the base of the second metacarpal (dorsoradial) and the radial shaft about 10 cm proximal to the styloid, between brachioradialis and ECRL. Spanning plate: distal incision over the second or third metacarpal and proximal incision over the dorsal radial shaft; the plate is tunnelled under the extensors.
approaches.interval: External fixator: blunt dissection to bone through open incisions with soft-tissue sleeves, proximal to where APL and EPB cross the radius. Spanning plate: tunnel deep to the second compartment (ECRL/ECRB) to the second metacarpal, or through the fourth compartment to the third metacarpal.

atRisk.why: Emerges between brachioradialis and ECRL at the proximal radial pin site. Use an open approach and sleeves for every half-pin; it is the main cause of pin-site neuroma.
The plate tunnel runs beneath the second compartment; keep the plate on bone so it does not trap the wrist extensor tendons.
Crosses the plate path near Lister's tubercle. Check that EPL glides freely after tunnelling and is not caught under the plate.
With the third-metacarpal plate through the fourth compartment, the plate lies beneath the digital extensors. Check finger flexion and extension for tethering before closing.

steps: Ligamentotaxis: longitudinal traction to restore length and radial inclination; correct residual tilt with intrafocal K-wires.
External fixator: two half-pins in the second metacarpal and two in the radial shaft, joined with a frame; add K-wires for articular fragments.
Spanning plate: slide the plate from distal to proximal, fix to the metacarpal and then to the radial shaft under traction; add percutaneous or limited open fixation of articular fragments.
Plan removal: fixator usually at about 6 weeks; spanning plate after union, typically about 12 weeks.
implants: Wrist-bridging external fixator with 2.5–3.0 mm metacarpal and 3.0–4.0 mm radial half-pins.
checks: PA: radial height and inclination restored.
Radiocarpal and midcarpal joint spaces not wider than normal (no over-distraction).
Lateral: carpus centred under the radius, volar tilt at least neutral.
Fingers flex fully on the table (over-distraction makes them stiff).

after.weightBearing: Light use of the hand for daily activities with immediate finger movement. No lifting or weight bearing through the wrist until there are signs of union, usually about 6 weeks. A dorsal spanning plate allows weight bearing through a platform crutch.
after.rehab: Full finger, elbow and shoulder movement from day one. After stable plate fixation, a removable splint and early wrist motion. In a cast, keep the wrist neutral with 3-point moulding, not forced palmar flexion, and consider removing it and mobilising at 4 weeks. A home exercise programme gives results similar to supervised therapy for most patients.
after.followUp: Nonoperative unstable fractures: radiographs at 1–2 weeks, only if re-displacement would change management. Operated fractures: wound review at about 2 weeks and radiographs at about 6 weeks. No routine radiograph when immobilisation is removed unless there is clinical concern. Refer to fracture liaison or falls services.
complications: Median nerve compression or acute carpal tunnel syndrome (18.5% after volar plating in WRIST).
Pin-site infection after K-wires or external fixation (about 23–26% in WRIST).
Loss of reduction in a cast after manipulation (13% needed fixation in DRAFFT2).
FPL rupture from a plate at or beyond the watershed line (Soong grade 1–2).
EPL rupture: after undisplaced fractures (vascular or attrition, a few weeks after injury) and from dorsal screw tips or dorsal plates.
Extensor and flexor tenosynovitis needing plate removal, more common with dorsal and combined plating.
Malunion with ulnar-sided wrist pain from a positive ulnar variance.
Complex regional pain syndrome and stiffness.
pitfalls: Volar lunate facet fragment not captured by a plate set too proximally, or by too short a distal row: the carpus subluxes volarly with the fragment. Check the teardrop angle and use a rim or hook construct.
Plate placed distal to the watershed line (Soong 1–2) risks late FPL rupture. Placing it proximal to the line keeps the tendon off the plate; remove a prominent plate after union if symptomatic.

Dorsal screw tips are hidden on the true lateral because of the dorsal ridge and Lister's tubercle. Use the skyline view and screws 2 mm shorter than measured; tines in the third compartment rupture EPL.
A 23° tilted lateral shows the ulnar distal screws but not the radial styloid screw; take a PA or tilted PA as well.
Missing DRUJ instability after fixing the radius: test it before leaving theatre.
Over-distraction with bridging fixation causes finger stiffness and CRPS-like pain.
